questions.q: How did the Prophet define a true Muslim, in the saying quoted in the editorial?
options: One from whose hands and tongue people are safe
Yes. A peaceful, harmless member of society.
One who prays longer than others
Not quite. The article says: One from whose hands and tongue people are safe.
One who has memorised the most
Not quite. The article says: One from whose hands and tongue people are safe.
One who has travelled to many lands
Not quite. The article says: One from whose hands and tongue people are safe.
questions.rationale: “A true Muslim is one from whose hands and tongue people are safe.”

questions.q: Science has fathomed only a small fraction of the universe. What does the article conclude about knowing the Creator?
options: To demand complete knowledge of God is unreasonable; man finds Him through realising his own helplessness
Well reasoned. We know “more and more about less and less.”
Only scientists can speak about God
Not quite. The article says: To demand complete knowledge of God is unreasonable; man finds Him through realising his own helplessness.
God cannot be known in any way
Not quite. The article says: To demand complete knowledge of God is unreasonable; man finds Him through realising his own helplessness.
Science will soon explain everything
Not quite. The article says: To demand complete knowledge of God is unreasonable; man finds Him through realising his own helplessness.
questions.rationale: “In this world a person can discover God only at the level of his helplessness and not at the level of absolute knowledge.”

questions.q: Tazkiya is usually rendered “purification.” What does the article say the word literally means, and what image does it use?
options: Rest – as night follows day
Not quite. The article says: Growth – as a seed in good conditions grows into a green tree.
Burning – as fire refines gold
Not quite. The article says: Growth – as a seed in good conditions grows into a green tree.
Growth – as a seed in good conditions grows into a green tree
Right. So it includes intellectual and spiritual development.
Washing – as rain cleans the dust
Not quite. The article says: Growth – as a seed in good conditions grows into a green tree.
questions.rationale: “Tazkiya literally means growth, one example of which can be seen in the tree.”

questions.article: Peace for the Sake of Peace
questions.q: “Peace is like rain.” What does the comparison mean?
options: Peace cannot be predicted
Not quite. The article says: Rain only waters the field – the farmer must sow and work; peace only opens opportunities, which people must use.
Rain only waters the field – the farmer must sow and work; peace only opens opportunities, which people must use
Yes. Peace is a means, not the end product.
Peace comes only in certain seasons
Not quite. The article says: Rain only waters the field – the farmer must sow and work; peace only opens opportunities, which people must use.
Peace falls equally on all without effort
Not quite. The article says: Rain only waters the field – the farmer must sow and work; peace only opens opportunities, which people must use.
questions.rationale: “Peace is like rain. Peace only provides you with the opportunities. It is up to people to avail of these opportunities by wise planning.”

questions.article: Between a Greater and Lesser Evil
questions.q: The article says that in life the choice is often not between right and wrong. Between what, then?
options: A lesser evil and a greater evil – and the wise choose the lesser
Correct. It prevents further loss and saves time for re-planning.
Friends and strangers
Not quite. The article says: A lesser evil and a greater evil – and the wise choose the lesser.
Two equally good courses
Not quite. The article says: A lesser evil and a greater evil – and the wise choose the lesser.
Speed and slowness
Not quite. The article says: A lesser evil and a greater evil – and the wise choose the lesser.
questions.rationale: “In this life the choice is not always between right and wrong. The choice is rather between the lesser evil and the greater evil.”

questions.article: Between a Greater and Lesser Evil
questions.q: “Others can create hurdles in your life, but…” How does the article complete the thought?
options: They can also remove them if asked
Not quite. The article says: No one has the power to decide your destiny; you can re-plan and reach your goal by another path.
No one has the power to decide your destiny; you can re-plan and reach your goal by another path
Well read. A closed road means others are open.
They will tire of it in time
Not quite. The article says: No one has the power to decide your destiny; you can re-plan and reach your goal by another path.
You must create hurdles for them too
Not quite. The article says: No one has the power to decide your destiny; you can re-plan and reach your goal by another path.
questions.rationale: “Although others can create hurdles in your life, no one has the power to decide your destiny. Your destiny is in your own hands.”

questions.q: What does the article identify as the basic theme of the Quran?
options: God’s creation plan: this life is a test, followed by an eternal life
Yes. “He created death and life so that He might test you.”
The history of ancient nations
Not quite. The article says: God’s creation plan: this life is a test, followed by an eternal life.
Rules of trade and government
Not quite. The article says: God’s creation plan: this life is a test, followed by an eternal life.
The geography of Arabia
Not quite. The article says: God’s creation plan: this life is a test, followed by an eternal life.
questions.rationale: “The basic theme of the Quran is the creation plan of God. All other subjects touched on by the Quran are related to this basic theme.”

questions.q: In a single word, what quality does the article say makes a person a deserving candidate for Paradise, “the home of peace”?
options: Ancestry
Not quite. The article says: Spirituality – a positive character free of anger, malice and dishonesty.
Learning
Not quite. The article says: Spirituality – a positive character free of anger, malice and dishonesty.
Spirituality – a positive character free of anger, malice and dishonesty
Right. Paradise suits only such a nature.
Fame
Not quite. The article says: Spirituality – a positive character free of anger, malice and dishonesty.
questions.rationale: “What are those qualities that are required for a person to be a deserving candidate for Paradise? In a single word, it is spirituality.”

questions.q: Why does the article compare the Prophet’s warning about the Hereafter to a hurricane forecast?
options: Because forecasts are often mistaken
Not quite. The article says: It concerns a coming reality we cannot alter; we can only prepare for it or be caught unprepared.
Because storms pass quickly
Not quite. The article says: It concerns a coming reality we cannot alter; we can only prepare for it or be caught unprepared.
It concerns a coming reality we cannot alter; we can only prepare for it or be caught unprepared
Well reasoned. It makes the matter personal and urgent.
Because it applies only to some regions
Not quite. The article says: It concerns a coming reality we cannot alter; we can only prepare for it or be caught unprepared.
questions.rationale: “If the meteorological department forecasts a hurricane, it is telling us about an impending disaster in which those affected will have no say in the matter… One can either escape or expose oneself to destruction.”

questions.q: Two men climbed into David’s chamber and put a case that was really an admonition to him. How did this powerful king respond?
options: He understood, sought God’s forgiveness at once, and did not punish or scold them
Exactly. He accepted correction, however it came.
He refused to hear them that day
Not quite. The article says: He understood, sought God’s forgiveness at once, and did not punish or scold them.
He had them arrested for trespass
Not quite. The article says: He understood, sought God’s forgiveness at once, and did not punish or scold them.
He asked his ministers to decide
Not quite. The article says: He understood, sought God’s forgiveness at once, and did not punish or scold them.
questions.rationale: “David enjoyed tremendous power at that time, but he did not punish or even scold the intruders… when his attention is drawn towards his shortcoming, he readily accepts it and rectifies it.”
